description:
Review finding from worktree-qzr2-wal-trim.

Problem:
ShardServer.start_link globally registers each process by shard_id alone. A running Shale log already owns a private Demux, and that Demux already keeps the authoritative shard_id-to-pid map used by Log.get_shard_server. No production consumer looks up a ShardServer through the global registry.

When replicated logs route the same shard, the first Demux creates the globally named ShardServer and later Demuxes receive already_started. Demux currently logs that creation failure and continues without recording the shard. A later cut can therefore take the no-shards durability path and report a floor to Shale even though that log replica never routed or persisted its shard data. Shale may then trim the only WAL copy owned by that replica.

Required design:
- Start every ShardServer anonymously as a private, linked child of exactly one Demux. The owning Demux map is its only process registry. Do not replace the current global key with a more elaborate global or per-log name.
- Keep durability state replica-local. A durability confirmation must apply only to the ShardServer incarnation owned by the receiving Demux.
- Treat every slicing error and every failure to create or route to a required ShardServer as fatal to the Demux. The link chain must fail the owning Shale log into normal recovery. Such a failure must never be converted into successful empty routing or a no-shards floor confirmation.
- Preserve the shared deterministic chunk namespace. Replicas continue using conditional create, and already_exists remains a successful confirmation because identical ordered inputs and cuts produce identical chunk bytes.

Scope:
This ticket changes ShardServer ownership and Demux failure semantics only. It does not change where transaction slicing occurs, introduce a Delivery envelope or special heartbeat classification, add object read-back or ETag verification, or namespace chunk objects by log replica.

Acceptance criteria:
- Production ShardServers have no global or Registry name; two Demuxes can independently own live ShardServers for the same cluster and shard_id.
- Log.get_shard_server still discovers the child through the selected log and its Demux and returns that replica-local pid.
- A ShardServer creation or routing failure terminates the Demux and owning Shale log without emitting a durability floor for the failed data path.
- A multi-log integration test uses two real Shale logs, separate WAL directories, and a shared controllable object backend. It proves both replicas receive the same shard data and own distinct ShardServer pids.
- The integration test holds one replica persistence operation, lets the other confirm, and proves the held replica cannot advance its floor or trim its WAL before its own confirmation.
- The confirmed owner can fail while the other replica is awaiting durability; the waiting replica remains independent, retains its WAL, and advances and trims only after its own persistence operation completes.
- Replica output is byte-identical for identical ordered inputs and cuts, so one conditional create may win and the other may confirm through already_exists.
title: Give every replicated log an independent ShardServer per shard
